transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I guess the main thing is that I've just stopped caring about everything I used to look forward to. My fishing gear is just sitting untouched out in the garage. I have a woodshop, but lately it just feels like a chore to even go out there. And even when my kids try to get me to play chess with them, I do it, but I'm really just going through the motions. I just don't have any interest in things right now.
How long have you been feeling this way—when did you first notice you stopped enjoying these activities?

Well, it's been... I'd say about a year and seven months now. That's when I first noticed it. It started right around the time my wife started having health problems. That just kind of changed everything at home for us, and I haven't really had much interest in anything since then.
Aside from this low period, have you ever had a distinct stretch of time—lasting a few days or more—when you felt unusually energetic, elated, irritable, or needed much less sleep than usual?
No... no, I haven't ever experienced anything like that. I've never really had a time where I felt super energetic or, you know, didn't need to sleep. It's pretty much just been this constant low.
Before this current period began about a year and seven months ago, had you ever gone through a separate episode of feeling this way—low mood and loss of interest—at some point earlier in your life?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had bad days or stressful weeks here and there, like anyone else, but nothing like this. This is the first time I've ever felt this... empty, and for this long. Before my wife got sick, I was always pretty steady.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep since this started—trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

Yeah, it's definitely changed. I mean, I can get into bed completely exhausted at night, but I just... I lie there running through bills and work schedules in my head. Or, if I do manage to fall asleep, I almost always wake up around three or four in the morning. After that, I can't get back to sleep. I just lay there staring at the ceiling until it’s time to get up and drive to the site.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that life isn't worth living?

Yeah... I have. On those early drives to the site, you know, before anyone else is even awake... I catch myself thinking it would just be easier if I didn't make it there. And sometimes, the thought of just steering off the road crosses my mind. It scares me, honestly, because it feels a little too close to actually doing it.
